key_insight: Lead-free AgBiS2 memristors can switch at ultra-low voltage and be tuned from digital to analog behavior by engineering thickness and interfaces, enabling controllable synapse-like operation.
engineering_relevance: This work points to a low-toxicity, solution-processable memristor platform for neuromorphic hardware with adjustable conductance dynamics and high ON/OFF performance.
method: First-principles calculations to identify favorable native defects and ion migration pathways in AgBiS2.
Device engineering of interface and switching-layer thickness to control abrupt versus gradual resistive switching.
Electrochemical and pulse-based measurements to probe ionic-electronic coupling and synaptic-like conductance modulation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an ultra-low SET voltage of about 0.08 V, an ON/OFF ratio greater than 10^4, and stable gradual conductance changes under pulse trains.
watch_item: Repeated filament formation and rupture cause substantial morphological evolution, which may affect long-term device reliability and switching variability.
paper_title: Controlling Switching Evolution in Lead-Free Perovskite-Inspired Chalcogenide Memristors for Neuromorphic Computing
